title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-09
korean_summary: 오늘 핵심: 공무팀 점검표 11시까지 받아 본사 소방 안전 보고(오늘 기한), 상사께 설비 이관 목록 확인·송부, 본사 계약서 사본 송부, 주간 연료 보고
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Monday, November ninth. This is your English briefing for Monday.
A new week starts today. There is one report due to head office today, two open items from last week, and a few replies to send. Let's get ready together.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a short practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. The fire patch status report for the head office compliance manager.

What is it? Fire patches are small sheets we put inside electrical cabinets and outlets. They stop a small fire from spreading. A head office manager from the compliance team asked for our fire patch status. The deadline is today.

You asked the maintenance leader to check every panel, socket and power strip in the factory. You also asked him to fill in a check sheet. The compliance officer already replied on Friday afternoon. She reported the stock. There are no sheets left for the cabinets. There are some small pieces for outlets. She also sent the price from the supplier.
But the check sheet from the maintenance leader has not come back yet. Without it, you cannot say how many places need a new patch.

Why is it important? Head office is watching fire safety closely. This morning, the head office compliance manager also replied to the HSE report from the compliance officer. HSE means health, safety and environment. The head office compliance manager asked her to replace one outlet right away and find the root cause.

Your first action today. Call the maintenance leader early and ask for the check sheet by eleven AM. Then put his numbers and the stock from the compliance officer together, and reply to the head office compliance manager before the end of the day.
Number two. The hanger line transfer to our sister factory.
What is it? My director asked for a list and a schedule to move the hanger lines to the sister factory. The deadline was Saturday, November seventh. In this morning's check, no reply email was found.

Why is it important? My director set the deadline himself. If it is late, he will ask about it. A manager at the sister factory is also asking about the payment for the hanger lines. Part of the payment may be made first.
Your first action today. Check whether the list was sent on Saturday. If not, send my director the list and the schedule this morning, and tell him the status of the payment.
Number three. The mending contract copies for a head office manager.

What is it? A head office manager looks after our records. He asked for a copy of the mending contract and the worker documents. Mending means fixing small problems on finished garments. The chief accountant sent you the files on Friday at five thirty PM.
Why is it important? This is about our records. Head office wants the papers to match the real work. The files are ready, so this is a quick win.
Your first action today. Open the files from the chief accountant, check that every page is clear, and send them to a head office manager this morning.
Part two. Reports to collect.
First, the check sheet from the maintenance leader. You need it for the fire patch report today. You can say:
Could you send me the fire patch check sheet by eleven AM today? I need it for the head office report.

Second, the October electricity invoices from the purchasing staff. Some V A T invoices are still missing. V A T means value added tax. They are for the sewing building, the finishing building and the security area. The water invoice for October is already in the file. The purchasing staff should also confirm the consumables ledger. You can say:
Just a reminder that the October electricity invoices are still missing. Please upload them by three PM today.

Third, the role check in the HR system. On Saturday morning, the HR manager said she finished entering the detailed role for each staff member. Foreign managers are not included. Please open the system and check a few records. You can say:
Thank you for entering the roles. I will check a few records today and let you know if anything needs to change.
Fourth, the stock count correction from the fabric warehouse leader. Items one and three were due on Saturday. Item two is due tomorrow, Tuesday. You can say:
Could you tell me the status of items one and three? Item two is due tomorrow.
Fifth, the purchase requests from accounting. On Saturday, several new purchase requests arrived for your approval. Some cash reports also arrived. Please review them before you approve. You can say:
I am reviewing the purchase requests now. I will get back to you on any questions by noon.
Part three. Replies you owe.

The first reply is to the HR manager about new sewers. You asked if we should hire sewers from other companies in December. The HR manager answered on Saturday. She thinks it is better to hire them after Tet. If they join in December, they work only two months before Tet. We may also have to pay part of a year-end payment for their time at another company. She does not have data to estimate how many people will come.
Your reply can start like this:
Thank you for the clear explanation. I agree that the timing matters. Before we decide, could you give me a rough estimate of the cost for each option?
The second reply is to the compliance officer about the C C T V and storage hard drives. On Friday, she asked for approval to replace them. Your reply can start like this:
Thank you for the request. Before I approve, please send me the list of the drives, their condition, and the quotation.
The third reply is to A manager at the sister factory about the hanger line payment. Your reply can start like this:
Thank you for waiting. I'd like to update you on the payment for the hanger lines.
The fourth reply is the weekly firewood report to a head office manager. Firewood is the fuel for our boiler. The report is due today. Your email can start like this:
Dear manager, please find attached the firewood usage report for last week.
Part four. The schedule and deadlines.
Today, Monday. The weekly firewood report to a head office manager. The fire patch report to the head office compliance manager. The hanger line list for my director, which is already late.
Tomorrow, Tuesday, November tenth. Short-term workers get their salary. Item two of the stock count correction from the warehouse leader is due.
Wednesday, November eleventh. The accountant will send the new fire insurance proposal. You will report it to my director after that.
Later this month. The collective labor agreement ends on November twenty-fourth. Please check with the HR manager this week that the renewal is on track.
Part five. English review.
Let's review expressions from today's card, from last Friday, and from last week.

The first expression is "oversee." It means to be in charge of something and watch it closely. For example, "From now on, the CAD leader will oversee the condition of the CAD room machines." Now say it with me.
One more time. The CAD leader will oversee the CAD room machines.
The second expression is "estimate." Here it is a noun. It means a rough number. For example, "Please give me an estimate of how many sewers may join and the total cost." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please give me an estimate of the total cost.
The third expression is "pending." It means until something is decided. For example, "Pending our decision, please do not wash the dummies." Now say it with me.
One more time. Pending our decision, please wait.

The fourth expression is a pattern. "To clarify, I'm asking about this, not just that." Use it when someone answers a smaller question than you asked. For example, "To clarify, I'm asking about sewers from other companies, not just former workers." Now say it with me.
One more time. To clarify, I'm asking about the total cost, not just the salary.
Now from last Friday. The pattern is "Going forward, please do this." It means from now on. For example, "Going forward, please use this file for every fire insurance renewal." Now say it with me.
One more time. Going forward, please send the check sheet every month.

The next one from last Friday is "It turned out that." Use it when you found the real reason later. For example, "It turned out that my PC had not synced the shared file. Sorry for the confusion." Now say it with me.
One more time. It turned out that the file was not updated.
And from last week. The word is "conduct." It means to carry out a check or a survey. For example, "We will conduct a physical count of fabric and thread on Saturday." Now say it with me.
One more time. We will conduct a check of all sockets.
The last one is "As far as I can see." It means based on what I checked. For example, "As far as I can see, the September costs are still empty in the ledger." Now say it with me.
One more time. As far as I can see, the check sheet has not come back yet.
Part six. A short role-play.
The situation. It is Monday morning. You call the maintenance leader about the fire patch check sheet.
Anthony: Good morning. Did you finish the fire patch check?
Leader: Good morning, Anthony. We checked the production floor and the warehouses. The dormitory and the office are not done yet.
Anthony: I see. Head office needs the report today. When will you be able to finish the rest?
Leader: We can finish by ten thirty.
Anthony: Great. Please send me the sheet by eleven AM at the latest. Did you find any burned or damaged outlets?
Leader: Yes. Two outlets on the sewing floor look damaged. We will replace them today.
Anthony: Thank you. Please also check the root cause, so it does not happen again. And please take a photo before and after.
Leader: OK. I will send the photos with the sheet.
Anthony: Perfect. Going forward, please check the outlets every month and tell me if any patch is missing.
Leader: Understood.
Now let's repeat two key sentences.
When will you be able to finish the rest?
Please send me the sheet by eleven AM at the latest.
Here is one more short role-play. You report the hanger line transfer to my director.
Anthony: Good morning. Do you have a minute? I'd like to update you on the hanger line transfer.
Director: Yes, go ahead. I asked for it by Saturday.
Anthony: I'm sorry it is late. I will send you the list and the schedule by email this morning.
Director: OK. What is the main point?
Anthony: The list shows each line, its condition, and the moving date. As far as I can see, we can finish the move within the planned period.
Director: And the payment?
Anthony: The sister factory manager asked about it. We are checking whether part of the payment can be made first. I'll get back to you on the payment by tomorrow.
Director: Fine. Please make sure the dates are clear.
Anthony: Yes. I will write the dates for each step, not "One day" or "Two days."
Now let's repeat two key sentences.
I'd like to update you on the hanger line transfer.
I'll get back to you on the payment by tomorrow.
Part seven. A short practice of key sentences.
Here are three sentences you will use today. Say each one after me.
Could you send me the fire patch check sheet by eleven AM today?
Here is the list and the schedule for the hanger line transfer. Sorry it is late.
I agree that the timing matters. Before we decide, could you give me a rough estimate of the cost?
Please find attached the mending contract and the worker documents you asked for.
Before I approve, please send me the list of the drives and the quotation.
Just a reminder that the October electricity invoices are still missing.

Now say them again, a little faster this time. First, the check sheet. Could you send me the fire patch check sheet by eleven AM today? Second, the hanger lines. Here is the list and the schedule. Third, the cost. Could you give me a rough estimate of the cost?
Part eight. The closing.

That's all for today. Let's say the one thing you must do today. Get the check sheet from the maintenance leader by eleven, and send the fire patch report to the head office compliance manager before the end of the day. Also send the hanger line list to my director and the contract copies to a head office manager this morning.
Have a good Monday, Anthony. See you this evening for tomorrow's briefing.
